awareness_subtitle: Think Before You Scan. Stay Safe Online.
hero_desc: Learn how QR scams work, recognize suspicious links, and protect your personal information and payments.

categories_desc: Practical, step-by-step guidance designed to empower everyday digital citizens against modern social engineering.

guide_a.title: QR Code Safety Basics
guide_a.desc: Understand what hides behind square barcodes and why appearance reveals nothing about destination safety.
points: What a QR code actually is: An optical 2D barcode that can encode URLs, Wi-Fi keys, text, or payment intents.
Visual deception: Every QR code looks similarly inert. You cannot judge safety from the black and white pixel pattern.
Physical overlay tampering: Fraudsters paste rogue stickers over legitimate signs in cafes, parking meters, and stations.
HTTPS is not proof of safety: Phishing attackers also use HTTPS encryption; TLS secures the pipe, not destination intent.
Inert inspection principle: Always preview and inspect the root domain before allowing your browser to open it.

guide_b.title: QR Phishing (Quishing) & Fake Login Pages
guide_b.desc: How cybercriminals use QR codes to harvest usernames, passwords, and multi-factor authentication tokens.
points: What is Quishing: QR-enabled phishing designed to bypass traditional text-based email spam filters and OCR scanners.
Psychological triggers: Attackers manufacture artificial urgency (e.g. 'Account suspended! Scan to verify in 24 hours').
Lookalike domains: Subtle character substitutions (typosquatting) designed to impersonate banks, HR portals, and streaming services.
Two-factor theft: Fraudulent pages that ask for immediate OTP entry to hijack active sessions.
Protective action: Never enter credentials on a page opened via a spontaneous or unsolicited QR code.

guide_c.title: UPI and Payment QR Safety
guide_c.desc: Essential precautions for scanning payment QR codes and avoiding common refund and merchant scams.
points: Receiving money NEVER requires your UPI PIN: Entering your UPI PIN always authorizes money leaving your account.
Verify recipient name and VPA: Always cross-check the payee name displayed inside your banking app before authorizing.
Dynamic amount injection: Fraudulent QR codes can pre-populate unexpected debit amounts.
Fake merchant standees: Scammers stick rogue QR stickers over shopkeeper payment stands.
Fake refund scams: Never scan a QR code sent over WhatsApp or SMS to claim a 'cashback' or 'lottery prize'.

guide_d.title: Suspicious URL Recognition
guide_d.desc: Learn how to spot deceptive domain structures, homograph attacks, and risky subdomains.
points: Understand registered domains: In 'chase.com.auth-update.xyz', the real website is 'auth-update.xyz', NOT Chase.
IP address hostnames: Legitimate public consumer portals rarely use raw IP addresses (e.g., http://192.0.2.1/).
URL shorteners: Services like bit.ly hide the actual endpoint. Use safe redirect inspection to preview where they lead.
Punycode homoglyphs: International characters that mimic standard Latin alphabet letters to deceive eyesight.
Suspicious ports: Web destinations using non-standard ports (e.g., :8080, :8443) should be treated with high caution.

guide_e.title: Wi-Fi QR Code Safety
guide_e.desc: How wireless connection QR codes work and why public Wi-Fi credentials require discretion.
points: Embedded network credentials: Scanning a Wi-Fi QR code automatically imports network SSIDs and WPA/WPA2 passwords.
Evil Twin attacks: Attackers set up rogue hotspots with names matching authentic public venues to intercept traffic.
Privacy discretion: Never upload or share QR codes containing private home or corporate Wi-Fi keys.
QShield masking: QShield automatically masks Wi-Fi passwords to prevent accidental shoulder-surfing and log leakage.

guide_f.title: Public QR Code Risks
guide_f.desc: Recognizing physical tampering on parking meters, restaurant tables, posters, and charging kiosks.
points: Tactile inspection: Feel the sign. Is there an adhesive sticker raised over the printed surface?
Parking & transport scams: Fake payment stickers pasted over legitimate parking payment signage.
Menu & table replacement: Counterfeit tabletop stands directing diners to fake ordering sites that harvest credit cards.
Official alternatives: When in doubt, manually type the organization's verified domain or use their official app store app.

guide_g.title: Privacy & Personal Information Protection
guide_g.desc: Understanding what data QR codes transmit and maintaining strict operational hygiene.
points: URL query tokens: URLs can embed private session IDs, user emails, or reset tokens in query parameters.
External reputation lookups: Threat intelligence checks share the URL with third-party feeds; QShield requires explicit consent.
Redirect tracing boundaries: Outbound redirect inspectors must enforce strict SSRF blocks against private networks.
In-memory processing: QShield processes QR images strictly in memory and discards image bytes after decoding.

guide_h.title: What to Do After Scanning a Suspicious QR
guide_h.desc: Immediate, practical recovery steps if you scanned an untrusted code or entered information.
points: 1. Disconnect immediately: Close the browser tab. Do not click 'Confirm', 'Cancel', or any button inside the page.
2. Change compromised passwords: If you entered credentials, immediately change your password on the genuine site.
3. Freeze payment instruments: If financial information was entered, contact your bank or UPI provider immediately.
4. Revoke active sessions: Check your online account security settings and click 'Log out of all other devices'.
5. Official cybercrime reporting (India): Report fraudulent transactions and quishing incidents at cybercrime.gov.in or call National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930.

scenarios_desc: Analyze realistic situations, identify red flags, and practice making the safest cybersecurity decision.

scenarios.title: Scenario 1: The Parking Meter Sticker
scenarios.situation: You park your car in a downtown municipal parking zone. On the parking meter, you see a shiny square sticker with a QR code and the text 'Fast Mobile Pay'. Looking closely, the sticker covers the original printed logo.
scenarios.question: What is the safest action to take?
options: Scan the QR code and pay quickly so you don't receive a parking ticket.
Avoid scanning the sticker. Use the physical payment slot or download the city's verified parking app from the app store.
Peel off the sticker to see what is underneath, then scan the peeled sticker.
scenarios.explanation: Sticker overlays on parking meters are a widespread scam. Fraudsters place fake stickers to steal credit card details or redirect parking fees to their own accounts. Always use official parking apps or payment machines directly.

scenarios.title: Scenario 2: The Urgent Account Suspension Letter
scenarios.situation: You receive a printed letter or email displaying your bank's logo. It warns: 'Your KYC has expired. Your account will be frozen in 12 hours. Scan this QR code immediately to complete facial re-verification.'
scenarios.question: How should you respond to this message?
options: Scan the QR code immediately to prevent your bank account from being frozen.
Treat the urgency as a major red flag. Do not scan the QR code. Open your bank's verified official app or visit your branch.
Reply with your account number and ask if the QR code is authentic.
scenarios.explanation: Banks never enforce urgent KYC re-verification via anonymous QR codes with artificial countdowns. Attackers use fear and urgency to trick users into entering credentials on lookalike pages.

scenarios.title: Scenario 3: Selling an Item Online & QR Payment
scenarios.situation: You listed an old sofa on an online marketplace. A buyer contacts you and says: 'I am sending you the money right now. Scan this QR code in Google Pay or PhonePe to receive the Rs 8,000 payment into your bank account.'
scenarios.question: What should you do?
options: Scan the QR code and enter your UPI PIN to accept the transfer.
Refuse to scan the QR code. You NEVER need to scan a QR code or enter a UPI PIN to receive money.
Ask the buyer to send a different QR code.
scenarios.explanation: This is India's most prevalent OLX/marketplace scam. In UPI architecture, receiving funds is completely passive; scanning a QR code or typing your UPI PIN will ONLY debit money from your account.

scenarios.title: Scenario 4: The Unfamiliar Public Wi-Fi QR
scenarios.situation: At an airport lounge, you see a laminated paper on a random table that reads 'Free High-Speed VIP Wi-Fi - Scan Here'. The cafe staff did not mention it, and the network SSID has a slight spelling variation from the official lounge name.
scenarios.question: What is the best course of action?
options: Scan the QR code to connect and immediately log into your company email.
Ask the official airport lounge staff for their verified network details and avoid scanning unsolicited tabletop codes.
Connect to the Wi-Fi and conduct banking transactions.
scenarios.explanation: Attackers place rogue Wi-Fi QR codes (Evil Twin hotspots) in airports and cafes to intercept unencrypted traffic and perform Man-in-the-Middle credential theft. Always verify wireless networks with staff.

scenarios.title: Scenario 5: The Subdomain Trick
scenarios.situation: You scan a QR code from a poster announcing an educational webinar. The URL preview shows 'https://google.com.webinar-portal-update.xyz/login'.
scenarios.question: Is this an authentic Google service?
options: Yes, because 'google.com' is written right at the beginning of the address.
No. The real domain is 'webinar-portal-update.xyz'. 'google.com' is merely a deceptive subdomain prefix.
Yes, because the URL starts with https://.
scenarios.explanation: Browsers navigate to the registered root domain immediately before the Top-Level Domain (TLD). Here, the root domain is 'webinar-portal-update.xyz', while 'google.com' is an unauthorized subdomain designed to mislead your eyesight.

scenarios.title: Scenario 6: The Festive Reward Coupon
scenarios.situation: You receive a postal envelope with a festival scratch card claiming you won Rs 25,000 in a brand lucky draw. It instructs you to scan a QR code to claim your prize, which opens a webpage asking for your debit card number and CVV.
scenarios.question: What is the safest step?
options: Enter your card details quickly before the offer expires.
Immediately discard the scratch card. Legitimate lotteries never require debit card numbers or CVVs to disburse awards.
Share the QR code with your friends so they can win too.
scenarios.explanation: Lottery scratch-card scams are designed to harvest financial instrument details. Never input card credentials, expiry dates, or CVVs to claim prizes.

checklist_heading: Before You Trust a QR Code (Interactive Checklist)
checklist_desc: Review these safety checks before scanning or interacting with an unfamiliar QR code in physical or digital spaces.
checklist_items: I recognize the physical or digital source that provided this QR code.
The physical sign or surface does not show signs of sticker tampering or overlay.
I inspected the decoded web address before allowing my browser to open it.
The root registered domain accurately matches the authentic organization.
The page does NOT request unsolicited passwords, OTPs, or credential re-entry.
For payment requests: I verified the payee VPA and amount inside my official payment app.
I understand that HTTPS encryption secures transmission but does not prove website legitimacy.
